text:
sara.nguyen: Thinking out loud — if we move GPU workloads to a Karpenter provisioner with AZ affinity + fractional pack policy, what happens to our burst capacity and cross-AZ traffic?

mike.chen: Good Q. AZ affinity will help keep pods local which reduces inter-AZ egress and speeds up PV attach. But could cause temporary binpacking in one AZ and underutilization in others.

julia.park: We observed that with our current cluster-autoscaler setup — one AZ hit ENI limits last week when training jobs spiked. That caused pending pods even though other AZs were idle.

navid.k: FYI I ran a quick sim this morning: moving to Karpenter with "consolidate: true" and the fractional gpu packing policy reduced node-hours by ~18% on a synthetic mix. But spot fallback behavior created fragmentation during scale-down.

ops-bot: @channel Reminder: any changes to provisioning policies should go through canary in staging first :rocket:

mike.chen: Example provisioner snippet I'm proposing (staging):
```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-burst-staging
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: kubernetes.io/arch
      operator: In
      values: ["amd64"]
    - key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-priority
      operator: In
      values: ["spot", "ondemand"]
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: 1000
      ephemeral-storage: 5Ti
      memory: 5Ti
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 300
  provider:
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: "redwood-prod-
    securityGroupSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: "redwood-sg"
```
(we'll param the subnet selector per-AZ)

sara.nguyen: That looks fine. Question: how do we handle the initial spike where training jobs want full GPUs (1 GPU per pod) vs inference which can be fractional? We can't over-pack full-GPU jobs.

julia.park: We tag pods with gpu-request: "full" and gpu-request: "fractional" in the scheduler constraint. Karpenter can use node labels to place fractional pods on quantized instance types (e.g., g5.2x -> 1 GPU) while full-GPU pods prefer g5.8x.\
navid.k: Also consider a small warm pool of on-demand g5.8x instances in each AZ to handle hot full-GPU spikes. Put them in Dedicated pool with a per-AZ cap so they don't overprovision. That avoids spot cold-starts causing failures.\
sara.nguyen: Warm pool cost estimate?

mike.chen: Rough numbers: a g5.8x on-demand ~ $8.50/hr in us-west-2. If we keep 3 per AZ across 3 AZs for hot jobs that's ~ $229/hr baseline. Versus spot-only approach that saved us 60% but had 5–7 min spinups sometimes.

julia.park: We can autoscale warm pool down during nights using a simple cron autoscaler. Cost can drop a lot off-hours.

navid.k: Network constraints: ENI per instance matters. For g5.8x we get X ENIs? (we need to map instance type to IP-per-pod limits). If we pack many fractional pods on a single instance we'll hit pod density vs ENI limits. Karpenter can place fewer instances but that increases ENI pressure.

mike.chen: True — fractional packing increases host-level pod counts. We should set maxPods and use CNI-aware node templates. Also consider using awsvpc-cni custom networking (prefix delegation) to increase pod density per ENI.

sara.nguyen: Another failure mode: consolidation TTL too aggressive + spot termination = churn. We saw increased scheduler evictions when TTL was 60s. navid, can you try 300s?

navid.k: Yup I'll run a 48h run with TTL 300, consolidation on, spot priority, and warm pool enabled. Watchlist: pod pending latency, number of node launches/hr, cross-AZ data egress.

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered: staging/provisioners/gpu-burst-staging.yaml by mike.chen at 1769992100

mike.chen: Also planning a metric export to Datadog:
- karpenter.node_launches.count
- karpenter.consolidation.evictions.count
- cluster.pod_pending_seconds.p95 (by AZ)
- aws.ec2.instance_spot_interruption.count

julia.park: Can we instrument per-tenant cost by tagging pods with tenant-id and having Karpenter propagate instance tags? That helps billing and identifying noisy tenants.

mike.chen: Karpenter supports node labels via provider.nodeTemplate — we'll add tenant-tags for long-running jobs. For ephemeral spot training, we rely on pod annotations to pass cost center to the monitoring pipeline.

sara.nguyen: One more: cross-AZ PVC attach. If we prefer AZ affinity, PVs must be accessible. Our default storage class is AZ-local. For jobs that move, we need S3-backed or CSI snapshots to avoid stuck pods.

navid.k: Agreed. For training checkpoints use S3 and mount via s3fs or better: use our model-checkpoint sidecar that streams to S3. Avoid PVCs for transient training.

mike.chen: Action items: 
1) navid: run 48h staging job with TTL=300, consolidation on, warm pool (3 per AZ) and report metrics by EOD Tuesday.
2) julia: add Datadog dashboards and per-AZ pod_pendings.
3) sara: update runbook for ENI exhaustion play (how to force cross-AZ spread).
4) ops-bot: schedule canary test window Thursday 09:00-12:00 PT.

sara.nguyen: Thanks. If staging looks good we'll run a limited prod rollout to one cluster (non-PRD) and monitor for 24h. :thumbsup:

mike.chen: I'll also add a small Canary job that slowly increases fractional packing to detect performance regressions.\
julia.park: Note for the doc: call out the tradeoff table — cost vs. latency vs. network risk vs. eviction churn.\
navid.k: Uploading logs and sim results to the thread (gist coming).

ops-bot: Canary scheduled for 1769999000 - 1769999800 (Thursday).

sara.nguyen: Great thread — keeping thread pinned for follow-ups.

navid.k: Report: 48h run finished. Preliminary: node launches down 16%, cross-AZ egress down 22%, eviction spikes only during spot interruptions. Full report in gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood-examples/abc123

mike.chen: Awesome, thanks navid. Next steps: tighten consolidation rules after we validate P95 pod startup.

sara.nguyen: closing loop: we'll cut the prod rollout Monday if no regression in canary.
